terra.problem: Paul being an apostle is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The passage does not say that without an interpreter nobody can tell what the speaker said.
The text says the person receiving the revelation is seated, but does not say the first speaker is standing.
Paul says everyone may be instructed and encouraged; the explanation turns that possibility into a guaranteed result.
The cookie-box comparison does not match taking turns, and cookies landing in one box do not establish that nobody goes home empty-handed.
It presents the Corinthian meeting as actually running in turns, rather than as the order Paul instructs them to follow.
The explanation is flat and repetitive: after the quote, its last two sentences simply restate that Paul points to the law.
Saying the person gets ignored 'back' suggests the ignored party does the ignoring in return. The text does not identify who will ignore the person.
The explanation is generic and repetitive, ending with 'He says what he says and moves on' rather than adding a distinct Papa Dorin voice.
